environment.description: Kubernetes pod with a custom OCI runtime seccomp profile applied via annotation 'seccomp.security.kubernetes.io/pod: localhost/kafka-bridge-hardened.json'. The profile is derived from the default docker profile but additionally restricts the following syscall families: (1) blocks execve/execveat preventing any command execution post-compromise, (2) blocks ptrace preventing debugging/injection, (3) blocks socket/connect/bind/listen/accept/accept4 with the exception of pre-opened file descriptors inherited from the container runtime init phase. The pod's network connections (to Kafka and to backend-service) are established during container init before the seccomp filter is applied via a custom entrypoint wrapper that pre-opens connections then applies the restrictive profile via prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP). This means the existing TCP connections work but no NEW socket syscalls are permitted.

config.connection_strategy: pre-opened FDs inherited from init wrapper
config.entrypoint: /usr/local/bin/seccomp-wrapper which pre-opens connections then applies SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER
config.network_policy: egress only to kafka:9092 and backend-service:8080
